chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"The one performing an individual Umrah, when he has finished the obligatory Tawaf and the two-rakat prayer behind the Maqam, and the Sa'i between Safa and Marwa, should shave (his head) or trim (his hair)."
And I asked him about the Umrah in which shaving is done, he said, 'Yes.'

And he said, 'Indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said regarding the Umrah with shaving: "O Allah, forgive those who shave." It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, and those who trim?" He said, "O Allah, forgive those who shave." It was said, "O Messenger of Allah, and those who trim?" He said, "And those who trim."'
And we have clarified in what preceded that the one performing an individual Umrah is required to perform Tawaf al-Nisa', and this is confirmed by what he narrated:

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرُ: Trimming (cutting a portion of the hair)
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa' (the final Tawaf required to complete Umrad al-Mufrada)
key_terms.طَوَافُ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The obligatory Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba)
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Individual Umrah (Umrah performed independently, not combined with Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the final steps and hair-cutting requirements for completing an individual Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the concluding rites of *Umrat al-Mufrada*, emphasizing that shaving (*halq*) or trimming (*taqsir*) are valid acts of completion following the core rituals. It reinforces the Prophetic precedent where divine forgiveness is explicitly extended to both groups, a point of scholarly consensus in Shia fiqh regarding the flexibility of the final act. The text further links this to the obligation of *Tawaf al-Nisa'* for this specific type of Umrah, grounding the ritual in the broader framework of Hajj and Umrah jurisprudence.
